subject: Post-call: Opsly model fit observations + emergency options
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Park <jared@opsly.ai>, Elena Soto <elena@opsly.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 09 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Opsly model fit observations + emergency options

Hi Jared / Elena —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we have a clear path forward: 

What we heard
- Main ask: reduce hallucination on invoice extraction and increase recall for vendor name fields in low-context prompts.
- You observed a subtle shift after a model rollout last night where vendor recall dropped ~6-8% on our sample prompts.

Redwood quick recommendations (next steps)
1) Short-term: Pin traffic to the previous model snapshot used on Nov 7 (redwood-8b-q4f@v20271107) for affected routes. This is a safe rollback and typically restores prior behavior while we investigate.
2) Eval pack: we attached the prompt set we ran and CSV snippets showing the diffs; please review opsly_promptset_v1.txt and opsly_eval_snippets.csv.
3) Medium-term: run a focused eval of redwood-11b-opt-pt and redwood-8b-q4f with aggressive prompt templating (we can share suggested system prompts).

Links / artifacts
- Shared benchmark dashboard: https://redwood-internal.corp/benchmarks/opsly/2027-11-08
- HubSpot deal record: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567

If you want us to proceed with an emergency pin/rollback, we need a go-ahead from you and an approximate maintenance window of ~30-45 minutes — we’ll minimize disruption. Rishi will own the rollback steps and Marcus will watch infra metrics.

Attachment(s): opsly_promptset_v1.txt (text, 12 KB), opsly_eval_snippets.csv (CSV, 48 KB)

Thanks — happy to jump on a 15-min call if you prefer an immediate live rollback.

—
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
hannah@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Jared Park <jared@opsly.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena@opsly.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 09 Nov 2027 10:03:21 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Opsly model fit observations + emergency options

On Tue, Nov 9, 2027 at 9:12 AM, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai> wrote:
> If you want us to proceed with an emergency pin/rollback, we need a go-ahead from you and an approximate maintenance window of ~30-45 minutes — we’ll minimize disruption.

Thanks Hannah — appreciate the quick plan.

We did notice the change starting ~02:00 UTC yesterday after your platform auto-deployed a newer variant (redwood-8b-q4f@v20271108). The most visible symptom is vendor name omission on short receipts. A quick example from yesterday:

--- sample request ---
input: "Merchant: ? (short receipt)"
expected: "Vendor: BayCity Coffee"
actual: "Vendor: Coffee"
--- end ---

This truncation causes downstream mismatches in our reconciliation steps. We’re happy to do a pin if that restores behavior. Please proceed with the rollback/pin as soon as you confirm you can do it safely. If you need my permission on a maintenance window, I can make myself available immediately.

Also attaching a screenshot of the failed parse and a short CSV of failing examples.

Attachment(s): screenshot-failure-20271108.png (PNG, 92 KB)

-Jared
Jared Park
Head of Data Engineering, Opsly
jared@opsly.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Park <jared@opsly.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 09 Nov 2027 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Opsly model fit observations + emergency options

Thanks for the quick example, Jared — that helped. Sequence proposal below.

Emergency action plan (recommended)
- Step 1 (immediate): Pin the affected route(s) to redwood-8b-q4f@v20271107. This is a config flip on our routing layer; no code change. Expected latency impact: negligible.
- Step 2 (monitoring): Marcus to verify token profiles and tail latency, plus run ~500 quick evals from opsly_promptset_v1.txt to confirm vendor recall restored.
- Step 3 (post-rollback): Capture a snapshot of model outputs and run a diff job (we’ll attach results as opsly_eval_snippets.csv).
- Step 4 (follow-up): If pin fixes behavior, we’ll schedule a controlled A/B test of redwood-11b-opt-pt with the same prompt instrumentation.

Notes / technical details
- Rollback CLI: redwood route pin --route opsly-invoice-parse --model redwood-8b-q4f@v20271107 --by rishi --reason "post-deploy regression 20271108"
- Expected time to completion: ~20-40 minutes including validation.
- Risk: low. If we need a full redeploy we’ll escalate, but we don’t expect it.

Attachment(s): rollback_playbook.pdf (PDF, 220 KB)

Requesting formal approval to proceed from Opsly (Jared or Elena) and confirmation from Hannah that we should run immediately.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 09 Nov 2027 13:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Opsly model fit observations + emergency options

Internal note / tasking only — Jared authorized immediate pin earlier (see thread). Please proceed with the plan and update HubSpot after rollback completes. Checklist below: 

Rollback checklist (assignments)
- Rishi: execute rollback CLI and paste run output to the HubSpot note.
- Marcus: run the 500-eval quick-run against redwood-8b-q4f@v20271107 and attach opsly_eval_snippets.csv. Watch infra metrics (token consumption + 95th pct latency).
- Hannah: notify Opsly when validation hits and confirm track-back remediation steps.

Acceptance criteria
- Vendor recall on the short receipt sample restored to baseline (within 2% of Nov 7 baseline).
- No >5% increase in 95th percentile latency.

I'll open a private support ticket for follow-up and schedule a 30-min postmortem tomorrow to review why v20271108 drifted. Link to HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567

Thanks — keep the thread updated in real time.

—
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
